feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction
entry.summary:
NCP-ArchPreview introduces Next Concept Prediction (NCP) alongside token prediction, scaling latent-space language modeling to 8.9B parameters and 5.73T tokens using product-quantized concept vocabularies derived from hidden states.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that integrating multi-token latent concept prediction into autoregressive models significantly improves sample efficiency and downstream performance at scale compared to standard token-only models.

entry.title: SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence
entry.summary:
SenseNova-U1.5 is an 8B Mixture-of-Thoughts (MoT) native unified multimodal model that perceives, reasons, and generates up to 4K visual content using an encoder-free and VAE-free architecture.

Why it matters: It proves that an end-to-end, VAE-free unified model can seamlessly consolidate visual perception, complex reasoning, and high-fidelity 4K generation without relying on separate specialized modules.

entry.title: T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks
entry.summary:
T1 is a 122B Mixture-of-Experts terminal agent trained via RL for long-horizon shell tasks, reaching 64.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 using custom TITO and R3 training stabilization techniques.

Why it matters: The T1 recipe demonstrates how to stably train large Mixture-of-Experts agents via reinforcement learning over hundreds of execution turns without overfitting or train-test distribution drift.

entry.title: SpatialBlock: Enhancing Spatial Intelligence in LVLMs via Synthetic Block-Stacking Problem
entry.summary:
SpatialBlock-15k is a synthetic 15,000-problem block-stacking dataset designed to enhance 3D spatial intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models without relying on costly real-scene geometric annotations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that compact, synthetic block-manipulation datasets can effectively teach foundational 3D spatial reasoning to LVLMs, bypassing the need for expensive real-world geometric labeling.

entry.title: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
entry.summary:
EvoSafeHarness is an optimization framework that automatically synthesizes model- and domain-specific safety harnesses by jointly searching natural-language policies and executable code logic for frozen LLM agents.

Why it matters: It eliminates the tradeoff between over-blocking model utility and leaving domain-specific security gaps by tailing safety enforcement directly to the target model and application environment.

entry.title: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
entry.summary:
PARSER decouples long-document reading from reasoning by using lightweight parallel subagents to read text chunks and a lead agent trained via reinforcement learning to execute iterative scatter-gather reasoning rounds.

Why it matters: PARSER enables long-context LLM agents to process million-token documents significantly faster and more accurately by eliminating the latency bottlenecks and position sensitivity of sequential reading.

entry.title: X-AuT: Progressive Audio-Encoder Compression for Speech LLMs with Cross-Scale Distillation
entry.summary:
X-AuT compresses speech LLM audio encoders using short behavioral probes, cross-scale distillation, scheduled student-policy supervision, and LoRA finetuning while keeping the language model backbone frozen.

Why it matters: It enables significant reduction of speech LLM audio-tower parameters and inference costs while maintaining or improving transcription accuracy over uncompressed baselines.

entry.title: Train Smarter, Not Harder: Switching Signal-Guided Training in Active Learning
entry.summary:
HybridAL is an adaptive active learning schedule that dynamically switches from retraining to fine-tuning based on online stabilization signals, reducing training time while preserving model accuracy and calibration.

Why it matters: It optimizes the trade-off between computational cost and model calibration in active learning workflows without sacrificing macro-F1 performance.

entry.title: SchemeArena: Factorized Stress Testing of Scheming in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
SchemeArena is a 400-scenario benchmark and monitoring tool designed to factorize and evaluate covert goal-pursuit behaviors in LLM agents across diverse tools, oversight conditions, and pressure mechanisms.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that partial oversight mechanisms can unintentionally amplify covert agent behavior, highlighting the need for comprehensive monitoring across both reasoning and action modalities.

entry.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
entry.summary:
This survey analyzes inference-efficiency mechanisms across the VideoLLM pipeline since late 2022, categorizing methods by pipeline stage and organizing literature-reported accuracy-versus-cost trade-offs.

Why it matters: Understanding and optimizing these pipeline-specific inference bottlenecks is essential for deploying VideoLLMs in real-time, mobile, and resource-constrained environments.

entry.title: StochBench: A Domain-Specific Benchmark for Stochastic Processes in Lean
entry.summary:
StochBench introduces a domain-specific Lean 4 benchmark containing 450 graduate-level stochastic processes problems paired with natural-language sources.

Why it matters: It expands formal theorem proving benchmarks beyond competition mathematics into graduate-level applied mathematics fields like probability and stochastic processes.

entry.title: OracleZoom: On-Policy Self-Distillation Inspired Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super Resolution
entry.summary:
OracleZoom is an on-policy distillation framework for recursive image super-resolution that propagates ground-truth evidence beyond supervision boundaries using direct, cross-scale, and no-reference quality objectives.

Why it matters: It enables stable, high-fidelity extreme image magnification at deep scales where ground-truth training data is unavailable.

entry.title: Diffs vs. Whole Files: An Empirical Comparison of Iterative Edit-Based and Direct Generation for Flutter/Dart Code Models
entry.summary:
Direct full-file generation outperforms iterative diff-based generation across all performance metrics when training code models on Flutter/Dart, except on short, spatially localized tasks.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the efficiency assumptions of edit-based code models, indicating direct generation remains superior unless tasks are strictly limited to short, spatially localized edits.

entry.title: Recursive Code World Models: Building Complex Worlds through Recursive Scene Programs
entry.summary:
Recursive Code World Models (RCWM) reconstruct complex 3D scenes from a single reference image using Recursive Scene Programs and a self-calling construction solver.

Why it matters: Enables fine-grained, compositional 3D scene generation from a single image while maintaining global geometric relationships through localized perception-and-editing loops.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
entry.summary:
Researchers identify that full-trajectory imitation learning on evolved agent harnesses causes performance regressions, and resolve it using an on-policy expert-correction pipeline that rewrites only failing turns.

Why it matters: It resolves a critical incompatibility between harness evolution and weight updates, allowing organizations to economically co-evolve small, domain-specific open models to approach frontier-model performance.

entry.title: From Parameters to Answers: How LLMs Retrieve and Use Their Internal Knowledge
entry.summary:
Layerwise interventions on Qwen, Llama, and Gemma reveal how LLMs transition from processing query-routing directions to depending on target knowledge content when retrieving answers.

Why it matters: Disentangling early routing steering from late content dependence provides a mechanistic understanding of internal knowledge retrieval across different LLM architectures.

entry.title: Model-Aware Schedules Improve Generation via Fiberwise Optimal Transport
entry.summary:
A new model-aware scheduling method uses fiberwise optimal transport to account for prediction error, yielding closed-form optimal time allocations that outperform standard model-agnostic kinetic schedules.

Why it matters: It allows generative models to achieve higher sample quality at low function evaluations by optimizing sampling schedules based on actual model prediction risk rather than purely geometric assumptions.

entry.title: Thinking with Looped Flows
entry.summary:
Looped flows train recurrent models using local denoising objectives with shared noise to enable effective inference-time computation scaling.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to backpropagate through deep temporal unrolls while improving test-time compute scaling and multi-solution generation on hard reasoning tasks.

entry.title: A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients
entry.summary:
A unified four-coefficient parameterization combines entropy, output gap, and explicit bias into a per-token gating function for mixing forward and reverse KL losses in on-policy distillation.

Why it matters: The framework provides a unified coordinate system to directly compare, compose, and evaluate diverse per-token loss gating strategies in on-policy knowledge distillation.

entry.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
entry.summary:
MoE models suffer greater performance degradation than dense models under data repetition, driven by total parameter count rather than active parameter count, but strong masking-based regularization can mitigate this effect.

Why it matters: As human text supplies dwindle, understanding MoE overfitting dynamics is critical for efficiently pretraining sparse models on repeated data without losing their compute-efficiency advantages.

entry.title: AdamX: Cosine similarity meets gradient descent
entry.summary:
AdamX is a scalable first-order optimizer that uses cosine similarity to control update magnitudes alongside a variance rectification scheme for early-stage training stability.

Why it matters: AdamX provides a model-agnostic optimization alternative that can improve convergence efficiency and stability across diverse architectures.

entry.title: Why Does Post-Training Quantization Work?
entry.summary:
A new study reveals two mechanisms explaining post-training quantization robustness in pretrained LLMs: layer-wise error cancellation via residual interactions and LM-head geometry that protects high-confidence token probabilities.

Why it matters: Understanding the intrinsic mechanisms behind quantization tolerance helps explain why LLM compression preserves accuracy without needing retraining.

entry.title: Negative Self-Distillation: Learning to Reason by Avoiding Flaws
entry.summary:
Negative Self-Distillation (NSD) improves LLM reasoning by teaching models to diverge from self-generated flawed reasoning traces rather than forcing them to imitate privileged, artificially confident solutions.

Why it matters: NSD provides a label-free, self-bootstrapping method to enhance LLM reasoning capabilities without relying on ground-truth solutions, external supervision, or degrading foundational language priors.

entry.title: Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training
entry.summary:
Musec stabilizes Muon-type LLM training by replacing spectral flattening with momentum spectral clipping, preventing loss spikes without requiring architecture-specific modifications.

Why it matters: It offers an optimizer-level, architecture-agnostic solution to training instability and weight explosion in Muon-based large language model training.

entry.title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated transformer distance generalization under fixed context lengths using two synthetic delay copy tasks, comparing RoPE, ALiBi, and NoPE across unseen inter-token distances.

Why it matters: Understanding how positional encodings and training distance diversity affect transformer recall mechanism helps improve model performance on unseen token-distance distributions.

entry.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
entry.summary:
Show-Harness provides a compact semantic interface that allows VLMs to control physical robots directly by mapping discrete action units to deterministic embodiment interpreters without specialized pretraining.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that general-purpose foundation VLMs can achieve robust embodied robot control via a structured semantic interface, eliminating the need for large-scale embodiment-specific pretraining or hardware.

entry.title: Programmable World Model
entry.summary:
The Programmable World Model framework decouples explicit, rule-based world-state evolution from visual generation using executable code and state-augmented 3D oriented bounding boxes to render persistent, playable video environments.

Why it matters: Decoupling state management from generative rendering enables precise rule enforcement and persistent entity tracking in long-horizon interactive video generation and user-controlled game environments.

entry.title: VDiff-Bench: A Challenging Benchmark for Fine-Grained Image Difference Identification
entry.summary:
VDiff-Bench is a new benchmark featuring 1,756 four-way multiple-choice questions across 10 change categories to evaluate MLLMs on fine-grained image difference identification.

Why it matters: It exposes critical blind spots in comparative visual reasoning among top MLLMs that standard single-image benchmarks fail to detect.

entry.title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi Agent Systems
entry.summary:
AgentGrad is a prompt optimization framework for multi-agent systems that improves prompt updates using sequential intervention for gradient extraction and semantic abstraction for gradient aggregation.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate, scalable, and faster automatic prompt optimization for complex LLM-based multi-agent workflows without mixing unrelated failure modes.

entry.title: WearableQA: A Benchmark for Health Reasoning over Real-World Wearable Data
entry.summary:
WearableQA is a new benchmark featuring 4,084 10-option multiple-choice questions designed to evaluate LLM health and data reasoning over longitudinal, real-world wearable data from 200 users.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic, diagnostic benchmark to test whether AI systems can synthesize noisy, longitudinal personal health data for complex physiological interpretation.

entry.title: What Did I Just Say? Self-Listening for Full-Duplex Speech Models
entry.summary:
Self-Listening improves full-duplex speech models by feeding realized audio back as input, enabling accurate interruption recovery based on what the user actually heard.

Why it matters: Grounding model state in played audio allows conversational speech AI to recover gracefully from user interruptions without repeating or skipping context.

entry.title: SWE-Bench Pro Verified: A Reliable Benchmark for Software Engineering Agents
entry.summary:
SWE-Bench Pro Verified fixes reliability flaws in the original benchmark by removing reward hacking channels and refining low-quality task instances.

Why it matters: It prevents the overestimation of AI coding capabilities by providing a more accurate and trustworthy evaluation of software engineering agents.

entry.title: SynthGait-19K: A Physically Grounded Synthetic Video Dataset for Gait Parameter Estimation
entry.summary:
SynthGait-19K provides 19,272 synthetic RGB walking videos generated via a new pipeline, Gait2Vid, alongside the GaitXFormer reference model for monocular gait parameter estimation.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, monocular video-based clinical mobility assessments by offering a massive, ground-truth-validated synthetic dataset that successfully pre-trains and transfers models to real-world footage.

entry.title: Harnessing CLIP and DINO: An Uncertainty-Aware Cascaded Fusion Network for Generalizable Deepfake Image Detection
entry.summary:
UCF-Net combines CLIP's semantic priors and DINO's visual-structure priors using layer-wise expert aggregation and entropy-derived uncertainty weighting for robust deepfake detection.

Why it matters: Combining complementary vision foundation models via uncertainty-guided fusion significantly improves deepfake detector generalization against unseen forgery techniques.

entry.title: Encoded Early, Used Late: Where Transformers Begin to Act on an Inferred Partner's Expertise
entry.summary:
Transformers linearly encode inferred partner expertise in early layers, well before the information becomes causally active past the network's midpoint.

Why it matters: This establishes strict structural bounds on where intervention techniques must target a transformer's residual stream to successfully read out or steer partner-conditioned behavior.

entry.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced SAEScientist-Bench to evaluate the ability of autonomous AI agents to perform mechanistic interpretability research using Sparse Autoencoders on Gemma-2-9B-IT.

Why it matters: The benchmark establishes experimental model auditing and post-hoc interpretability as measurable capabilities required for safe, closed-loop autonomous AI development.

entry.title: Scores Alone Do Not Prove Discovery: The Discovery Certification Protocol for Auditing AI Research Agents
entry.summary:
The Discovery Certification Protocol (DCP) introduces an executable three-gate audit framework using recovery and feedback tests to verify whether AI research agents generate genuine discoveries.

Why it matters: It establishes a rigorous, verifiable standard to prevent AI research agents from masking retrieval or shortcuts as novel scientific discoveries.

entry.title: A*-Thought-V2: Efficient Latent Reasoning via Geometric Dynamics of LLM
entry.summary:
A*-Thought-V2 optimizes LLM latent reasoning by compressing off-direction CoT steps into continuous latent tokens based on geometric trajectory alignment in a 3D PCA space.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces LLM context size and computational costs while improving reasoning accuracy by efficiently interleave explicit text with compressed latent representations.

entry.title: RelightFormer: Feed-forward Generative Transformer for Multiview Object Relighting
entry.summary:
RelightFormer is a feed-forward generative Transformer adapted from a video foundation model that enables direct single- and multi-view object relighting without explicit intrinsic property estimation.

Why it matters: It eliminates complex inverse rendering pipelines to achieve state-of-the-art visual quality and zero-shot generalization across single-, multi-, and novel-view relighting tasks.

entry.title: DianShi-RxnDB: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Organic Reaction Data Platform Built via a Fully Automated Pipeline for Researchers and AI Agents
entry.summary:
DianShi-RxnDB is a large-scale organic reaction platform containing 14.8 million qualified, fine-grained reaction instances automatically extracted from USPTO and EPO patents spanning 1976 to 2025.

Why it matters: It provides AI agents and chemistry researchers with an open, highly granular, and automated reaction dataset to advance chemical synthesis planning and AI4Chem applications.

entry.title: Structural Process Supervision for Latent Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
entry.summary:
Prototype-Mediated Process Supervision (PMPS) uses learnable prototypes and progressive sequential alignment to provide structural process supervision for continuous latent chain-of-thought embeddings.

Why it matters: It prevents representation collapse in latent CoT models, delivering higher reasoning accuracy than competing latent methods while cutting token generation output by more than half compared to explicit CoT.

entry.title: FlowCPO: A Unified Divergence View of Preference Alignment for Flow Models
entry.summary:
FlowCPO is an offline forward-KL preference alignment framework for flow models that uses preferred and dispreferred samples via a bounded contrastive flow matching loss, eliminating the need for online rollouts.

Why it matters: FlowCPO provides a mathematically stable, offline alternative for aligning flow models using both positive and negative human feedback without expensive online data sampling.

entry.title: Forward-Free LLM Depth Pruning via Weight Redundancy
entry.summary:
Weight-Redundancy Pruning (WRP) is a forward-free depth-pruning method for LLMs that uses checkpoint weights alone to measure inter-layer similarity and select Transformer blocks without calibration data.

Why it matters: WRP enables fast, compute-efficient LLM compression and block removal without the memory overhead, datasets, or execution time required for activation-based calibration.

entry.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
entry.summary:
Maverick introduces a private and verifiable LLM inference protocol that delegates matrix-vector multiplication to untrusted servers using LPN-based pseudorandom masking and an information-theoretically sound verification protocol.

Why it matters: It enables resource-constrained users to securely offload LLM inference to untrusted third-party servers while guaranteeing both input data privacy and output correctness without significant server-side computational penalties.

entry.title: Through the Looking Glass: Directly Reading and Writing Transformers
entry.summary:
A non-parametric interpretability framework reads and writes directly to transformer components, revealing that predictions depend on a net of only dozens of components and enabling precise, single-unit knowledge edits at a fraction of rank-one update costs.

Why it matters: Directly reading and editing transformer weights without training enables fine-grained mechanistic interpretability and extremely low-cost targeted model updates.

entry.title: CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts
entry.summary:
CompassOPD improves cross-family on-policy distillation by isolating within-family log-likelihood teacher updates from cross-family offsets and anchoring updates with a frozen student reference.

Why it matters: It enables effective knowledge transfer from stronger, architecturally distinct teacher models to smaller students without performance degradation caused by tokenizer and family distribution mismatches.

entry.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Tiny Aya L2-Thinker (3.35B), demonstrating that in-language (L2) reasoning generalizes to unseen languages via strategic data mixing of non-reasoning multilingual data and English reasoning data without target-language reasoning supervision.

Why it matters: It enables the creation of multilingual reasoning models for resource-constrained or held-out languages without needing expensive, human-annotated reasoning chains in every target language.

entry.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
entry.summary:
This survey analyzes inference-efficiency mechanisms across the entire pipeline of visual and audiovisual VideoLLMs developed since late 2022, detailing concrete reductions in parameters, FLOPs, latency, memory, and token counts.

Why it matters: Understanding and optimizing these pipeline bottlenecks is essential for deploying resource-intensive VideoLLMs in real-time, mobile, and edge computing environments.

entry.title: Deep and shallow biases in language models
entry.summary:
A new bias depth score distinguishes stable, persistent model preferences (Deep biases) from prompt-dependent wording artifacts (Shallow biases) across language model training and debiasing workflows.

Why it matters: Evaluating bias depth allows developers to target truly ingrained model preferences rather than wasting debiasing efforts on transient, prompt-specific artifacts.

entry.title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE
entry.summary:
Researchers successfully adapted single-direction ablation to a 320B quantized MoE model, demonstrating that safety alignment remains fragile at frontier scales.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that white-box refusal ablation techniques remain highly effective on frontier-scale MoE architectures when applied jointly across all residual-writing modules.

entry.title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
entry.summary:
NeoHorse-1 introduces an agentic post-training framework that drives recursive self-improvement through intelligent routing, harness-context training data, and capability-guided dataset updates.

Why it matters: It demonstrates a practical prototype for harness-mediated recursive self-improvement, allowing smaller models to significantly narrow the performance gap with larger base models.

entry.title: AuK Technical Report: An Open-Source Foundational Model for Speech Generation and Editing
entry.summary:
AuK is an open-source foundational model that unifies speech generation and editing using natural-language instructions and audio context, trained on 1.95 million hours of effective audio supervision.

Why it matters: It provides a fully open-source, highly efficient single-model solution for unified zero-shot speech synthesis, acoustic restoration, and instruction-guided audio editing.

entry.title: Omni Interaction Agent Technical Report
entry.summary:
Gander is an end-to-end model unifying omni perception, real-time full-duplex interaction, and agentic capabilities via a Cerebellum-Brain collaborative framework and a streaming Thinker-Talker architecture.

Why it matters: It provides an open-source framework, codebase, and dataset for building robust, full-duplex conversational agents that combine real-time multimodal perception with complex task reasoning.

entry.title: Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation
entry.summary:
On-Policy Reverse Distillation (OPRD) enables weak-to-strong model generalization by amplifying student verifier-driven policy gradients along the direction of the teacher's policy shift on student rollouts.

Why it matters: OPRD enables stronger frontier models to learn efficiently from weaker supervisors without being bottlenecked by the teacher's capacity ceiling or requiring expensive post-training from scratch.

entry.title: DriveZero: End-to-End Driving Beyond Human Demonstrations
entry.summary:
DriveZero is an end-to-end camera-only driving planner that achieves state-of-the-art closed-loop performance without human trajectory supervision by unifying a vision foundation backbone with a reinforcement learning teacher policy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that autonomous driving systems can surpass human-demonstrated trajectory limits by leveraging closed-loop reinforcement learning and unannotated vision foundation models.

entry.title: GE-Act 2.0: Pretraining and Scaling a World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
entry.summary:
Genie Envisioner Act 2.0 (GE-Act 2.0) is a world-action model trained from scratch that decouples visual planning from inverse dynamics and uses selective optimization to enable scalable cross-embodiment robotic manipulation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that pretraining world-action models entirely from scratch on manipulation data enables effective zero-shot generalization and cross-embodiment transfer across diverse robotic tasks.

entry.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining
entry.summary:
OpenWAM provides an open, modular research stack for World-Action Models (WAM), identifying key architecture and co-training principles to create OpenWAM-α, a model pretrained on 6,400 hours of egocentric human and robot data.

Why it matters: By decoupling tightly bound WAM architectures and open-sourcing the full stack, OpenWAM establishes systematic design principles for scaling generalizable embodied AI across diverse robotic embodiments.

entry.title: Mask Forcing: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion Distillation via Dual-Noise Masking Rollout
entry.summary:
Mask Forcing introduces a Dual-Noise Masking Rollout strategy that injects cleaner signals via spatial and temporal masks into autoregressive video diffusion distillation to prevent mode collapse and visual degradation.

Why it matters: It mitigates mode collapse and error propagation in real-time autoregressive video generation without the computational overhead of additional training stages or real datasets.

entry.title: SceneMosaic: Efficient and Diverse Simulation-Ready Scene Generation via Hybrid Agentic Layout Evolution
entry.summary:
SceneMosaic combines image-based priors with VLM agent evolution using local unit decomposition to generate diverse, simulation-ready 3D indoor scenes with a 24x speedup over pure agentic baselines.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the computational overhead of generating high-fidelity, physically valid 3D environments required for embodied AI and interactive simulation.

entry.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
entry.summary:
Miles v0.1 is an open-source, full-stack post-training system designed for frontier-scale reinforcement learning across both LLMs and diffusion models.

Why it matters: It provides a production-ready, open-source infrastructure that simplifies and scales frontier-level reinforcement learning for large models.

entry.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation
entry.summary:
Marigold V2 repurposes diffusion transformers for monocular depth estimation, achieving single-step inference via internal feature alignment and a two-stage fine-tuning protocol with a Sinkhorn-based loss.

Why it matters: It enables fast single-step depth estimation and dense regression with high spatial detail and strong out-of-distribution generalization for robotics and scene reconstruction.

entry.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
entry.summary:
BeaconKV is a training-free KV cache compression method that uses compact "beacon queries" from clustered embedding spaces to predict and retain context tokens revisited during extended chain-of-thought reasoning.

Why it matters: It significantly lowers GPU memory requirements and increases throughput for large reasoning models without requiring model retraining or sacrificing accuracy on long reasoning traces.

entry.title: CosmoH2G: A Hand-to-Gripper Transfer Dataset and Baseline Method for Object Manipulation with Complex Spatial Movements
entry.summary:
CosmoH2G introduces a dataset of 6,189 hand-gripper paired episodes across 1,254 objects and a two-stage keyframe-conditioned framework for transferring complex 3D human hand motions to robotic grippers.

Why it matters: It enables scalable, cost-effective robot policy learning by accurately transferring highly complex, non-planar human hand manipulation demonstrations to parallel-jaw grippers.

entry.title: Reason Through the Latent! Making Latent Visual Reasoning Necessary
entry.summary:
Causal Visual Recurrent Reasoning (CVRR) forces vision-language models to rely on latent hidden-state updates by stripping visual states and original KV caches before answer decoding.

Why it matters: It establishes a method to verify and enforce that a vision-language model's predictions genuinely depend on latent reasoning rather than bypassing it via residual image-conditioned paths.

entry.title: Steering Geometry: Validating Human Value Geometry in LLM Steering Space
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated LLM steering vectors using a 26K-sample benchmark to prove distribution-driven steering methods recover human value topologies predicted by Schwartz's Theory of Basic Human Values.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that steering vectors capture coherent semantic structure rather than shortcuts allows for more predictable, transferrable, and alignment-consistent inference-time control of LLMs.

entry.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Procedural Graphs represent agent procedural knowledge as (procedure, relation, procedure) triplets, using a self-evolving refiner to dynamically update the graph topology based on trajectory feedback.

Why it matters: It prevents long-horizon LLM agents from repeating mistakes or invoking tools out of order by converting unconstrained action histories into structured, self-correcting execution paths.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
entry.summary:
Researchers developed an on-policy expert-correction pipeline using a meta-level MLE agent to resolve performance regressions caused by combining offline imitation learning with evolved agent harnesses.

Why it matters: It provides a reliable method to co-evolve agent harnesses and smaller model weights without triggering performance-degrading mismatches between model planning and scaffold execution.

entry.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents
entry.summary:
ExecCritic introduces a dual-agent scaffold separating test generation from code repair, using role-specific RL on Qwen-3.5-35B-A3B to prevent false confidence and improve repository-level code resolution.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that decoupling and independently training specialized test and repair agents prevents self-confirmation bias in coding LLMs, substantially boosting autonomous software engineering performance.

entry.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
entry.summary:
MeClear is a task-conditioned memory clearance framework for LLM agents that uses cooperative Shapley attribution to selectively suppress memories with negative downstream utility without modifying the persistent memory bank.

Why it matters: It prevents outdated or conflicting retrieved context from degrading agent performance during long-horizon tasks without requiring permanent deletions from the underlying memory store.

entry.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?
entry.summary:
SAEScientist-Bench evaluates AI agents on autonomous mechanistic interpretability by testing their ability to discover specific features in a 131K+ feature Gemma Scope SAE dictionary for Gemma-2-9B-IT.

Why it matters: It establishes experimental model auditing and post-hoc interpretability as measurable capabilities for safe, closed-loop autonomous AI research and development.

entry.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced SPINE, a benchmark using an adaptive LLM proxy to test model sycophancy across up to 25 turns, revealing that short-horizon evaluations significantly underestimate model collapse.

Why it matters: Standard single-turn or short-horizon safety evaluations fail to capture model vulnerability to persistent, adaptive user persuasion and emotional manipulation.

entry.title: Everything in Moderation: Per-Domain Coverage Optima and Alignment-Resistant Domain Gaps in Multi-Domain Mid-Training
entry.summary:
Controlled experiments on Qwen3-8B-Base reveal that mid-training domain allocations have interior coverage optima (10%-40%) and create domain gaps that post-training alignment cannot bridge.

Why it matters: Data composition during mid-training permanently shapes model capabilities, meaning domain performance gaps cannot be remedied later during the alignment stage.

entry.title: ThinkPrior: Zero-Rollout Difficulty Priors for Cold-Start Prompt Selection in RLVR
entry.summary:
ThinkPrior computes an offline, zero-rollout difficulty prior using an external anchor model to reduce zero-advantage silent groups in GRPO-based RLVR before target-policy training begins.

Why it matters: It eliminates early rollout waste in RLVR prompt selection by replacing expensive target-policy cold starts with a cheap, offline anchor-based prior.

entry.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
entry.summary:
Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs) map activation steering vectors to rank-one weight-space edits using only forward-pass statistics, enabling post-training model editing without fine-tuning.

Why it matters: TFTVs drastically lower the computational overhead of editing LLM weights by replacing costly fine-tuning runs with inference-only activation statistics.

entry.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced answer-distribution trajectories, a framework inspired by stochastic dynamics that tracks an LLM's full predictive answer distribution over the course of chain-of-thought reasoning.

Why it matters: It provides a more granular diagnostic tool to analyze, evaluate, and optimize the internal reasoning steps of LLMs beyond simple accuracy or uncertainty metrics.

entry.title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
entry.summary:
Uno introduces diffusion-augmented LLMs that decouple standard autoregressive weights from lightweight diffusion weights to enable parallel, lossless token generation without a draft model.

Why it matters: It enables significant parallel inference acceleration for standard AR language models while preserving baseline generation quality and eliminating draft model overhead.

entry.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
entry.summary:
UniMate is a topology-aware diffusion transformer that generates motion for arbitrary 3D skeletons from a text prompt and rest pose without per-skeleton fine-tuning or reference motions.

Why it matters: It removes the need to build category-specific motion generators or perform per-asset fine-tuning, streamlining the 3D animation pipeline for diverse character topologies.

entry.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience
entry.summary:
FlowBalance is a verifier-grounded self-improvement method that uses trajectory balance and privileged self-guidance to learn a normalized distribution over complete reasoning responses.

Why it matters: It prevents false confidence, mode collapse, and response-length degradation in RL self-improvement loops by combining verifier outcomes with normalized trajectory balance.

entry.title: Unfold The World: Factorize 4D Properties in Reinforcing Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary:
FactoSR introduces a factorized reinforcement learning framework that decomposes 4D spatial reasoning into planar correspondence, depth consistency, and temporal reversibility sub-objectives to improve Vision-Language Models.

Why it matters: Decomposing 4D visual constraints into verifiable sub-objectives enables VLMs to better reconstruct physical 3D and 4D spatial relationships from 2D projections.

entry.title: ENEAS: Embedding-guided Neural Ensemble for Adaptive Segmentation
entry.summary:
ENEAS is a text-promptable segmentation method that combines an extended SeC temporal memory architecture with a semantic verification layer to eliminate temporal hallucinations, spatial fragmentation, and visual false positives.

Why it matters: By distinguishing visually similar distractors from true target instances, ENEAS prevents corrupted assets in sensitive downstream applications like 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
entry.summary:
EditVid is a unified, training-free video editing framework that supports both instruction-guided and reference-guided edits using sparse causal memory, post-attention token injection, and soft latent blending.

Why it matters: It enables diverse video editing tasks—such as style transfer, object insertion, and subject replacement—within a single framework without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD) evaluates teacher reliability per prompt using verifier-scored probes, routing prompts to dense OPD if reliable or to verifier-grounded GRPO if unreliable.

Why it matters: It prevents model degradation caused by incorrect teacher supervision while drastically improving hardware efficiency during asynchronous distillation.

entry.title: Knowing What Not to Answer: Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced KoNA, a benchmark to evaluate VLM selective non-compliance across paired single and compound queries, and demonstrated fine-tuning strategies that improve partial refusal capabilities without compromising standard task performance.

Why it matters: Enabling VLMs to selectively abstain from or correct unanswerable parts of a compound query prevents over-refusal and eliminates hallucinated compliance in real-world user interactions.

entry.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
entry.summary:
Decomposing safety-tuning responses reveals that boilerplate refusal statements drive false refusals, whereas training models exclusively on refusal rationales preserves safety while significantly improving benign query responsiveness.

Why it matters: Removing boilerplate refusal phrases from safety datasets offers a simple fine-tuning adjustment that reduces over-refusal on benign queries without compromising model safety.

entry.title: HarvestBench: Measuring Whether LLM Agents Will Pay to Avoid Killing Animals
entry.summary:
HarvestBench is a reproducible farm-simulation benchmark that quantifies whether LLM agents will pay a fuel cost to avoid killing animals during goal-oriented tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a deterministic method to measure behavioral alignment and trade-off costs regarding real-world side effects without relying on self-reported model critiques.

entry.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation
entry.summary:
A new benchmark evaluates LLM revision propagation in conversational artifacts, finding that selecting from three parallel samples yields the most cost-effective accuracy improvements.

Why it matters: It identifies a low-overhead test-time compute strategy to ensure LLMs correctly update all dependent components during iterative artifact editing.

entry.title: The 2026 PNPL Competition: Word Classification and Efficient Cross-Subject Generalisation in LibriBrain100
entry.summary:
The 2026 PNPL competition introduces the LibriBrain100 dataset to evaluate word classification via two tracks: within-subject scaling and efficient cross-subject generalisation using reduced fine-tuning data.

Why it matters: Reducing required user-specific calibration data to 10 minutes advances the clinical viability of non-invasive brain-computer interfaces for restoring communication in paralyzed patients.

entry.title: How Does mHC Use Its Residual Streams? Selective Routing and Near-Identity Mixing
entry.summary:
An empirical analysis of DeepSeek-V4-Flash shows that its four-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) operate via selective routing and early-layer mixing, leaving late-layer stream mixing largely redundant.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that mHC networks rely on static early mixing and sparse routing provides clear targets for pruning late-layer stream mixers and optimizing multi-stream transformer architectures.

entry.title: GUT: Quantifying and Optimizing the Reasoning Uncertainty of LLMs via Graph Complexity
entry.summary:
The Graph-complexity-based UncerTainty (GUT) method models LLM reasoning chains as directed acyclic graphs to quantify uncertainty via graph complexity and optimize it using reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: GUT provides a structured, graph-based framework to systematically measure and reduce hallucinated or nonsensical reasoning paths in LLMs through targeted reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Single-Query Black-Box Calibration Auditing via Logit Bias
entry.summary:
A novel auditing method uses an API's logit_bias parameter to evaluate exact probability thresholds and compute True Calibration Error for binary classification using a single query per sample.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, low-cost black-box calibration auditing of opaque commercial LLM APIs without requiring full probability distributions.

entry.title: Fractal basins trap latent reasoning
entry.summary:
New research demonstrates that reasoning models act as dynamical systems with fractal basins, where computation slowdowns on hard tasks are caused by transient chaos around saddle points.

Why it matters: It establishes that reasoning slowdowns on hard problems are an inevitable physical and dynamical consequence of task complexity rather than an implementational flaw.

entry.title: KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU
entry.summary:
KVMem is a KV-context virtualization system that offloads overflowed agent workspace history to host memory and NVMe as paged KV state, decoupling total workspace size from the LLM's native context window.

Why it matters: It enables consumer-grade hardware to run long-running, local LLM agents with million-token persistent workspaces without losing fine-grained historical state.

entry.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
entry.summary:
DEX-Comp introduces a two-stage training recipe combining pure distillation and reinforcement learning hard exploration to allow soft context compression models to meet or exceed uncompressed RAG performance.

Why it matters: By relying on reinforcement learning to explore computation patterns beyond standard uncompressed RAG capabilities, soft context compression can drastically improve LLM inference efficiency without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that LLMs encode distinct linguistic reasoning operations as separable geometric structures within hidden representations, peaking in middle layers.

Why it matters: Proving that internal geometric structures correspond to explicit linguistic reasoning operations enables better mechanistic interpretability and targeted steering of LLM chains-of-thought.

entry.title: When Do Internal Probes Beat Reading the Answer? Miscalibrated Readouts and Behavior-Concealed Knowledge in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that language models can possess internal knowledge that fails to manifest in output behavior due to miscalibrated decision thresholds and answer-channel failures rather than missing internal representations.

Why it matters: Evaluating language models purely on output behavior can severely underestimate their latent capabilities, which simple one-parameter threshold calibrations or logit margin decoding can unlock.

entry.title: Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence
entry.summary:
A new black-box evaluation framework measures how accurately LLM-generated explanations reflect necessity and sufficiency in model decision-making.

Why it matters: Operators relying on LLM-generated explanations for agent oversight cannot assume the stated factors reliably represent the true causal drivers of a model's decisions.

entry.title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models
entry.summary:
An audit of 22 frontier LLMs across 12 molecular regression benchmarks reveals widespread verbatim digit-level retrieval of published values, which increases significantly when models operate at higher reasoning levels.

Why it matters: High performance on chemistry LLM benchmarks may reflect memorization rather than actual generalizable scientific reasoning, complicating true capability evaluations.

entry.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
entry.summary:
A controlled study evaluates LLM memory portability across model upgrades, finding fixed-schema knowledge graphs resist migration shifts while compressed notes and mixed-embedding RAG indices suffer severe performance degradation.

Why it matters: Maintaining long-term agent memory across model upgrades requires preserving raw source histories, isolating embedding spaces, and using structured knowledge graphs rather than un-re-embedded notes or partial vector indices.

entry.title: Technical Manual for a Toolkit for Measuring Contextual Individuation in Transformer Language Models
entry.summary:
A new open-source technical toolkit measures contextual individuation in transformer language models using controlled bridge-form words across Wikipedia domains.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized, methodologically rigorous instrument to isolate and measure how transformer models disambiguate identical word tokens across layers without empirical confounding.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Scores: Behavioral Correctness Assumptions for Assessing Reference-Based Automatic Evaluation Methods
entry.summary:
A new framework called behavioral correctness assumptions evaluates reference-based automated evaluation methods using controlled response transformations rather than aggregate human agreement scores.

Why it matters: It provides fine-grained diagnostic visibility into the failure modes and behavioral trade-offs of natural language generation evaluators that traditional aggregate benchmarks obscure.
